FBS-036 - Browser-verify runner extension: blueprint-shipped probe pack loader, scoping predicate, aggregate verdict and --probe-pack CLInotStarted

FBS-036 - Browser-verify runner extension: blueprint-shipped probe pack loader, scoping predicate, aggregate verdict and --probe-pack CLI

Summary: T-0 of the ratified visual round (spec 2026-09-04, section 2.1): the browser-verify runner extension that lets a blueprint ship a Playwright probe pack under `blueprints/<slug>/probe-packs/` and have `rcf verify browser` discover, scope-check and run it as a required ship gate. Six ACs span the loader (schema + `.pack.js` and `.pack.mjs`), the applicability predicate (source-scan for one of the three legal scoping seams: route, tacIds or `blueprint:` tag), the check-id cross-check against the shipping blueprint's contributed AC ids, the runner pass (after invariants and auth-smoke, packs receive an injected browser and fetch), the aggregate verdict extension (block on any `severity: block` pack fail), the `--probe-pack <name>` CLI restriction, and the optional `preChecks[]` fast-fail slot with `dependsOn` skip semantics. Zero new npm dependencies; the pinned Playwright MCP the launcher provisions is the browser access seam. Unblocks T-1..T-5 (datatable, charts, dashboard, notifications-in-app, admin-console).

AC-1701-1AC-1701-2AC-1701-3AC-1701-4AC-1701-5AC-1701-6AC-1701-7AC-1701-8

Acceptance criteria delivered

AC-1701-1 - The pack loader discovers `.pack.js` and `.pack.mjs` modules under `blueprints/<slug>/probe-packs/` for every applied blueprint, imports each with a dynamic ESM import, validates the exported default object against the pack schema (`packName` starts with the owning blueprint's slug and matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, `version` semver, `blueprintSlug` matches the directory, `checks[]` non-empty with each entry carrying `id`, `severity` in {block, warn, advisory}, `description` and async `run`), and refuses at load (exit 2) with a diagnostic that names the pack path and the offending field on any violation. A valid pack registers on the run.

AC-1701-2 - The applicability predicate `appliesTo({ fbs, uiBaseline, manifest })` is a required top-level field on every pack; its source (`appliesTo.toString()`) MUST reference at least one of `route`, `tacIds`, or the `blueprint:` US-tag prefix, and an unqualified predicate (a body that references none of the three, including the default `() => true`) is refused at load with exit 2 and a diagnostic that names the pack, the requirement and the three legal scoping seams. A pack whose `appliesTo` returns `false` for an FBS records `applicable: false` on the record for that FBS with a one-line reason drawn from the predicate context and no `run` function is invoked.

AC-1701-3 - The loader cross-checks every `checks[].id` against the AC ids the pack's blueprint contributes through `blueprint.json:contributions[]` (reading each US contribution file and enumerating `acceptanceCriteria[].id`). A pack whose check names an AC id the blueprint does not contribute is refused at load (exit 2) with a diagnostic that names the pack, the offending check id and the AC ids the blueprint actually contributes.

AC-1701-4 - The runner runs the pack pass after invariants and after auth-smoke on `agentScreenshotCritique` mode. For each applicable pack the runner invokes every check's `run({ browser, fetch, runtimeUrl, route, theme })` (browser and fetch injected by the runner), records `{ id, verdict, severity, detail? }` on the pack record, and appends the pack record to `browserVerification.probePacks[]` on the composed record. The aggregate verdict extends the existing rule: `block` on any pack check whose severity is `block` and verdict is `fail`; `warn` on any pack check whose severity is `warn` and verdict is `fail` (and no block from invariants, auth-smoke or pack); `pass` otherwise.

AC-1701-5 - `rcf verify browser <fbs-id> --probe-pack <name>` restricts one run to one pack by name; a `--probe-pack` value that resolves to no discovered pack (nothing loaded under any applied blueprint's `probe-packs/` matches the name) exits 2 with a diagnostic that names the value and the packs that were discovered. When omitted, every discovered and applicable pack runs; when a pack's `appliesTo` returns false for the FBS, the pack record carries `applicable: false` and no browser check runs against it.

AC-1701-6 - A pack MAY declare `preChecks[]`: an array of `{ id, description, run: async () => ({ verdict, detail? }) }` Node build-scan fast-fail checks that the runner invokes before any browser check on the same pack. A pre-check with verdict `fail` records on the pack record and every browser check that names it under `dependsOn` records verdict `skipped` with detail `skipped-by-pre-check:<preCheckId>`; browser checks with no `dependsOn` on a failing pre-check still run. Pre-check verdicts fold into the aggregate the same way pack checks do (a `fail` at `severity: block` blocks ship).

AC-1701-7 - The `packBrowser` seam the runner injects into every pack check is a real headless browser provisioned through the pinned Playwright MCP server (`PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VERSION` in `src/verify/engine/launcher.js`, spawned as `npx -y @playwright/mcp@<pin>` over stdio) via a thin in-package JSON-RPC 2.0 client (zero new npm dependencies in rcf-lite; no LLM call). Every check receives a stable API: `goto(url)`, `snapshot()` returning accessibility-tree text, `evaluate(fn, arg?)` returning a parsed value, `click(selector, hint?)`, `type(selector, text, hint?)`, `press(key)`, `screenshot(filename?)`, `close()`. When the consuming project already resolves `playwright` from its own `node_modules`, the runner MAY take that cheaper direct route and expose the identical API; the pinned MCP version remains the source of the browser otherwise. The CLI provisions the browser only when at least one applicable pack is loaded and `--no-browser` was not passed; `deps.packBrowser` on the CLI handler overrides the provisioning for tests.

AC-1701-8 - A pack MAY declare a `boot: { bootCommand, waitForUrl, waitForSelector }` object. Before running the pack pass, the CLI probes the runtime URL; when it responds with any HTTP status the boot is skipped and the running server is used unchanged. When the runtime is not answering AND `boot.bootCommand` is a non-empty string, the CLI spawns `bootCommand` from the project root (Node.js child_process, cwd=projectRoot, no shell), polls `waitForUrl` at a bounded interval until a timeout, and when the URL responds runs the packs; when `waitForSelector` is set and a browser is available, the CLI navigates the browser to `waitForUrl` and polls the accessibility snapshot for a substring match on the selector until a bounded timeout (soft-failure only, packs still run). The CLI stops any process it started in reverse order after the pack pass completes (SIGTERM then SIGKILL fallback after 3s). `--no-boot` disables the fallback and forces packs to run against whatever the runtime URL currently answers. When the runtime is unreachable AND no `bootCommand` is declared, the CLI records the note and proceeds; the pack's own runtime checks then surface the failure.

Applies cleanly (validate 0, coverage strict 0, eval strict 0 on a scratch project). Consumes T-0's runner extension.

TS-037 - `rcf define blueprint remove-resolution <adr-id>` verb: remove + idempotent + refuse behavioursdraft

TS-037 - `rcf define blueprint remove-resolution <adr-id>` verb: remove + idempotent + refuse behaviours

Verifies user story: US-1204

Purpose: Cover the single AC on US-1204: the ratified three-behaviour surface (remove entry, idempotent re-run, refuse-exit-2 on malformed or unknown id) end-to-end through the CLI, plus the help block advertising the verb.

Test level: integration

Acceptance criteria verified

AC-1204-1

Status: draft

Test cases

TC-037-remove-drops-entry-and-prints-line - covers AC-1204-1 pending

One resolutions[] entry seeded with resolvedByAdrId 'ADR-011-health-probes'; the verb prints the removal line naming the id, topic 'healthProbes' and resolution id, exits 0, drops the single entry from manifest.resolutions[], and leaves every other manifest section and the ruling ADR file on disk unchanged.

Test pointer: test/blueprint/cli.test.js::rcf blueprint remove-resolution drops the resolutions[] entry and prints one result line (spec A2)

TC-037-idempotent-second-run - covers AC-1204-1 pending

After a successful remove, a second run of the same command exits 0 and prints the 'nothing to remove' line without writing the manifest.

Test pointer: test/blueprint/cli.test.js::rcf blueprint remove-resolution is idempotent on re-run when the ruling ADR still exists on the tree

TC-037-refuse-malformed-adr-id - covers AC-1204-1 pending

A malformed id 'not-an-adr' exits 2 with the well-formed-ADR-id error on stderr.

Test pointer: test/blueprint/cli.test.js::rcf blueprint remove-resolution refuses exit 2 on a malformed <adr-id>

TC-037-refuse-unknown-adr-id - covers AC-1204-1 pending

A well-formed id ('ADR-999-nowhere') that names no ADR on the tree and no resolutions[] entry exits 2 with the 'is not a resolution entry' error on stderr.

Test pointer: test/blueprint/cli.test.js::rcf blueprint remove-resolution refuses exit 2 when <adr-id> is well-formed but names no ADR anywhere on the tree

TC-037-help-lists-verb - covers AC-1204-1 pending

`rcf help define blueprint` output contains the `remove-resolution <adr-id>` verb block including the idempotent-on-re-run line.

Test pointer: test/blueprint/cli.test.js::rcf help define blueprint prints the remove-resolution verb

TS-046 - Blueprint-shipped probe pack loader, scoping, cross-check, runner pass and CLI --probe-packdraft

Test level: unit

Acceptance criteria verified

AC-1701-1, AC-1701-2, AC-1701-3, AC-1701-4, AC-1701-5, AC-1701-6, AC-1701-7, AC-1701-8

Status: draft

Test cases

TC-046-pack-loader-loads-both-pack-js-and-pack - covers AC-1701-1 pending

Pack loader loads both .pack.js and .pack.mjs; validates packName pattern and blueprint-slug prefix; refuses non-array checks[] with exit 2 diagnostic

Test pointer: test/browser-verify/pack-loader.test.js::loadProbePacks accepts .pack.js and .pack.mjs and reports one loaded pack per legal module

TC-046-applicability-predicate-source-scan - covers AC-1701-2 pending

Applicability predicate source-scan refuses unqualified predicate () => true and refuses a predicate that references none of route, tacIds, blueprint:; appliesTo returning false records applicable=false

Test pointer: test/browser-verify/pack-loader.test.js::applicability predicate refuses unqualified default and records applicable=false when appliesTo returns false

TC-046-loader-refuses-at-exit-2-a-pack-whose - covers AC-1701-3 pending

Loader refuses at exit 2 a pack whose checks[].id names an AC id the blueprint does not contribute; the diagnostic names the offending id and the contributed AC ids

Test pointer: test/browser-verify/pack-loader.test.js::loader refuses a pack whose check id names an AC the blueprint does not contribute

TC-046-runner-pack-pass-invokes-each-check-s - covers AC-1701-4 pending

Runner pack pass invokes each check's run with injected browser and fetch, folds results into probePacks[], and aggregate verdict extension blocks on severity block fail and warns on severity warn fail

Test pointer: test/browser-verify/pack-runner.test.js::runProbePacksForFbs folds probePacks[] onto the record and the aggregate verdict extension blocks on a block-severity pack fail

TC-046-cli-probe-pack-option-restricts-to-one - covers AC-1701-5 pending

CLI --probe-pack option restricts to one pack by name; unknown name exits 2 with a diagnostic naming the discovered packs; when omitted every discovered pack runs

Test pointer: test/cli/browser-verify-probe-pack.test.js::rcf verify browser --probe-pack restricts to one pack and exits 2 on unknown pack name

TC-046-prechecks-runs-before-browser-checks-a - covers AC-1701-6 pending

TC-046-pack-browser-evaluate-parser - covers AC-1701-7 pending

The Playwright-MCP stdio client parses browser_evaluate result blocks (both the '### Result' fenced form used by MCP 0.0.80+ and the legacy 'Result:' trailer) into typed JS values so a pack's check can assert on the value directly

Test pointer: test/browser-verify/pack-browser.test.js::parseEvaluateResult returns a parsed JSON value when the MCP block ends with Result: <json>

TC-046-boot-skips-when-runtime-reachable - covers AC-1701-8 pending

bootIfNeeded returns already-up when the runtime URL responds with any HTTP status; returns no-boot / no-boot-command when the pack declares no boot / no bootCommand; spawns bootCommand and reports started when the URL flips to reachable; SIGTERMs the child on stop()

Test pointer: test/browser-verify/boot.test.js::bootIfNeeded spawns bootCommand, polls until waitForUrl responds, then reports started

TS-047 - application-datatable v1.0.0 shelf shape and probe pack cross-check

Verifies user story: US-1801

Purpose: Cover AC-1801-1..5 via unit tests over the shipped application-datatable blueprint's contribution counts (six REQs, nine USs, three TACs, four ADRs, 27 ACs total), the pack-loader accepting the shipped pack file with every check id cross-checked against the blueprint's contributed AC ids, the pack schema accepting the pack's applicability predicate (references route and tacIds), and the sample-app fixture's exported startServer plus /api/rows shape.

Test level: unit

Acceptance criteria verified

AC-1801-1, AC-1801-2, AC-1801-3, AC-1801-4, AC-1801-5

TS-048 - application-charts v1.0.0 shelf shape and probe pack cross-checkdraft

TS-048 - application-charts v1.0.0 shelf shape and probe pack cross-check

Verifies user story: US-1901

Purpose: Cover AC-1901-1..5 via unit tests over the shipped application-charts blueprint's contribution counts (four REQs, six USs, two TACs, three ADRs, 15 contributions total), the pack-loader accepting the shipped pack file with every check id cross-checked against the blueprint's contributed AC ids and every check carrying a description, the pack schema accepting the pack's applicability predicate (references route and tacIds), the sample-app fixture exporting startServer serving a chart route with two-series bar and line charts (colour plus pattern plus direct label) and a text-alternative table with keyboard focus and reduced-motion suppression, and the negative-run behaviour on the ?break=table, ?break=pattern and ?break=keyboard switches.

Test level: unit

Acceptance criteria verified

AC-1901-1, AC-1901-2, AC-1901-3, AC-1901-4, AC-1901-5

Status: draft

Test cases
